name: Carbon Composition
description: One of the oldest resistor types. Made from a solid cylindrical resistive element with embedded wire leads. They have high tolerance variance but handle high-energy pulses well.

name: Carbon Film Resistor
description: Constructed by depositing a carbon film on a ceramic core. They are widely used in general-purpose circuits, offering better stability and lower noise than composition resistors.

name: Metal Film Resistor
description: Formed by vacuum-depositing a metal layer on a ceramic substrate. They are highly accurate, boast low thermal noise, and are heavily preferred in precise analog/audio circuitry.

name: Metal Oxide Resistor
description: Similar to metal film, but uses metal oxide (like tin oxide). These offer significantly higher operating temperatures and excellent stability under high-stress environments.

name: Wire-Wound Resistor
description: Made by wrapping a resistive wire around a non-conductive core. Designed explicitly for massive power dissipation (up to hundreds of watts) in industrial settings.

name: Thick Film Resistor
description: Produced by printing a resistive paste onto a ceramic base. Very cost-effective and commonly used in massive-scale consumer electronics and standard SMD packages.

name: Thin Film Resistor
description: Manufactured using vacuum deposition. They offer incredibly tight tolerances and low temperature coefficients compared to thick film variations.

name: SMD Resistor
description: Surface-Mount Devices designed to be soldered directly onto the surface of a PCB. Essential for modern, compact, ultra-dense circuit board manufacturing.

name: Potentiometer
description: A three-terminal variable resistor with a sliding contact that forms an adjustable voltage divider. Widely used for volume knobs and user calibration.

name: Rheostat
description: A two-terminal variable resistor used to heavily control current flow in a circuit. Usually built to handle strictly larger currents than a standard potentiometer.

name: Trimmer (Preset)
description: A miniature variable resistor explicitly designed for 'set-and-forget' calibration inside circuit boards. Usually adjusted with a precision screwdriver.

name: Varistor (VDR)
description: A Voltage Dependent Resistor physically alters its resistance based on the applied voltage. Highly deployed to strictly protect circuits against transient voltage spikes.

name: Magneto Resistor
description: A solid-state resistor whose internal resistance drops or increases severely based on the intensity of an external magnetic field.

name: Strain Gauge
description: A sensor heavily utilized in mechanical engineering. Its electrical resistance predictably fluctuates depending directly on the amount of mechanical strain or deformation it undergoes.
